speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. Agent; you're here because of dizziness and vertigo, correct? To help narrow this down, have you noticed any hearing changes, tinnitus, or a feeling of fullness in your ear on the affected side?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail. Since the dizziness is sudden and position-dependent, do you notice any specific head movements—like rolling in bed, looking up, or bending down—that trigger the spinning sensation? Also, have you experienced any recent headaches, double vision, slurred speech, or limb weakness during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of sudden, position-dependent vertigo in an elderly patient with no other neurological deficits is classic for BPPV. I recommend a Dix-Hallpike maneuver for confirmation.
